'''Emma Haruka Iwao''' (born April 21, 1984) is a Japanese [[computer scientist]] and cloud [[Platform evangelism|developer advocate]] at [[Google]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> In 2019 Haruka Iwao calculated the then world record for most accurate value of [[pi]] (π); which included 31.4 trillion digits, exceeding the previous record of 22 trillion.<ref name=:0/><ref name=twitter>{{twitter}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JvEvTcXF-4Q|website=youtube.com|title=Beating the record of most-calculated digits of pi|publisher=[[YouTube]]|author=Anon|year=2019}}</ref><ref name=seattle>{{cite web|title=  Woman sets world record in Seattle for calculating the value of pi to 31.4 trillion decimal places |date=2019  |publisher=[[Seattle Times]] |url= https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/a-calculating-woman-sets-a-world-record-in-seattle/ |first=Nicloe |last=Brodeur|website=seattletimes.com}}</ref><ref name="washpo">{{Cite news |last=Shaban |first=Hamza |date=2019-03-14 |title=A Google employee just shattered the record for Pi calculations. Her name is Emma Haruka Iwao |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2019/03/14/google-employee-breaks-guinness-world-record-calculating-trillion-digits-pi/ |access-date=2024-11-15 |newspaper=[[Washington Post]]}}</ref> This record was surpassed in 2020 by Timothy Mullican who calculated 50 trillion digits,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://numberworld.org/y-cruncher/news/2020.html#2020_1_29|title=The Pi Record Returns to the Personal Computer|access-date=30 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.timothymullican.com/calculating-pi-my-attempt-breaking-pi-record|title=Calculating Pi: My attempt at breaking the Pi World Record|date=26 June 2019|access-date=30 January 2020}}</ref> but she reclaimed the record in 2022 with 100 trillion digits.<ref name=Iwao2022>{{Cite web |last=Iwao |first=Emma Haruka |title=Calculating 100 trillion digits of pi on Google Cloud |url=https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/compute/calculating-100-trillion-digits-of-pi-on-google-cloud/ |access-date=2022-06-15 |website=Google Cloud Blog |language=en}}</ref> The record was surpassed by a computer storage company in 2024, reaching roughly 105 trillion digits.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baker |first=Harry |date=2024-03-15 |title=Pi calculated to 105 trillion digits, smashing world record |url=https://www.livescience.com/physics-mathematics/mathematics/pi-calculated-to-105-trillion-digits-smashing-world-record |access-date=2024-04-11 |website=Live Science |language=en}}</ref> She identifies as [[queer]].<ref name="pink">{{Cite news |url=https://www.pinknews.co.uk/2019/03/18/google-queer-female-pi-tech-record-breaker-inspire-lgbt-community/ |work=PinkNews |date=18 March 2019 |title=Queer Google's queer female pi world record breaker hopes to inspire LGBT community |first=Ella |last=Braidwood}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
As a child, Iwao became interested in pi, learning of the record-breaking computations of her Japanese compatriots [[Daisuke Takahashi (mathematician)|Daisuke Takahashi]] and [[Yasumasa Kanada]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-47524760|website=bbc.com|publisher=[[BBC]]|title=Woman smashes pi world record|last=Kleinman|first=Zoe|date=2019-03-14|access-date=2019-03-14|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=NPR2019>{{Cite web |title=The Woman Who Calculated 31 Trillion Digits Of Pi |author=Francesca Paris |work=[[NPR]] |date=14 March 2019 |access-date=11 December 2025 |url=https://www.npr.org/2019/03/14/703566696/the-woman-who-calculated-31-trillion-digits-of-pi |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190314234135/https://www.npr.org/2019/03/14/703566696/the-woman-who-calculated-31-trillion-digits-of-pi |archive-date=14 March 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> She studied [[computer science]] at the [[University of Tsukuba]], where she was taught by Takahashi.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.blog.google/products/google-cloud/most-calculated-digits-pi/|first=Mia|last=Neagle|title=A recipe for beating the record of most-calculated digits of pi|date=2019-03-14|website=blog.google|language=en|access-date=2019-03-14}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.google.cn/intl/en/events/developerdays2017china/speakers/|title=Google Developer Day|website=google.cn|access-date=2019-03-14|archive-date=2019-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190304062755/http://www.google.cn/intl/en/events/developerdays2017china/speakers/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Dean's Award for Excellence]] in 2008, before starting graduate studies in computing. Her master's thesis considered high performance computer systems.<ref name=":2" /> After graduating, Iwao took on several software engineering positions, working on site reliability for [[Panasonic]], [[Gree (Japanese social network)|GREE]] and [[Red Hat]].<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Iwao joined [[Google]] as a Cloud Developer Advocate in 2015.<ref name=":0" /> She originally worked for Google in Tokyo, before moving to [[Seattle]] in 2019.<ref name=linkedin/> Iwao offers training in the use of the [[Google Cloud Platform]] (GCP), as well as supporting application developers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://software.intel.com/en-us/events/hpc-devcon/2017/hands-on-tutorials|title=Hands-on {{!}} Intel® HPC Developer Conference|last=mad\djchilsx|date=2017-11-10|website=software.intel.com|publisher=[[Intel]]|language=en|access-date=2019-03-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lesbianswhotech.org/speakers/emma-haruka-iwao/|title=Emma Haruka Iwao|author=Anon|year=2019|website=lesbianswhotech.org|publisher=Lesbians Who Tech|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-14|archive-date=2019-03-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330032519/https://lesbianswhotech.org/speakers/emma-haruka-iwao/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/pi-world-record-google-employee-emma-haruka-iwao-calculating-31-trillion-digits/|first=Christopher|last=Brito|year=2019|title=This Google employee just smashed the world record for calculating pi|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-14|work=[[CBS News]]}}</ref> She works to make [[cloud computing]] accessible for everyone, creating online demos and teaching materials.<ref name=cnn>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/03/14/tech/pi-day-record-google/index.html|title=A Google employee just broke the world record for calculating pi|last=Kelly|year=2019|first=Heather |website=cnn.com|publisher=[[CNN]]|access-date=2019-03-14}}</ref>

In March 2019 Iwao calculated the value of [[pi]] to 31,415,926,535,897 digits (equal to {{math|1= {{floor|''{{pi}}''&nbsp;×&nbsp;10<sup>13</sup>}}}}), using 170 [[terabyte]]s (TB) of data.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|first=Tom|last=Herbert|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/tech/google-emma-haruka-iwao-calculates-pi-to-world-record-a4091796.html|title=A Google employee has smashed the Pi world record... on Pi Day|date=2019-03-14|website=standard.co.uk|publisher=[[Evening Standard]]|location=London|language=en|access-date=2019-03-14}}</ref><ref name=guinness>{{Cite web|url=http://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/66179-most-accurate-value-of-pi|author=Anon|year=2019|title=Most accurate value of pi|website=guinnessworldrecords.com|publisher=[[Guinness World Records]]|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-03-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/business/ct-biz-google-pi-day-record-calculation-20190314-story.html|title=Pi Day news: Google employee breaks record, calculates 31.4 trillion digits of Pi|last=Shaban|first=Hamza|year=2019|website=chicagotribune.com|publisher=[[Chicago Tribune]]|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-14}}</ref> The calculation used a [[Multithreading (computer architecture)|multithreaded]] program called [[y-cruncher]] using over 25 machines for 121 days.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.numberworld.org/y-cruncher/|title=y-cruncher - A Multi-Threaded Pi Program|website=numberworld.org|access-date=2019-03-14|first=Alexander J. |last=Yee|year=2019}}</ref><ref name=cnn/> This was the first time the record had been set using a cloud computing service, and was achieved at a cost of roughly US$200,000.<ref name=IwaoYee2019>{{Cite AV media |author1=Emma Haruka Iwao |author2=Alexander Yee |title=CMP300: How We Broke the World Record for Computing Digits of Pi (31.4 trillion!) |minutes=7:33 |date=13 April 2019 |access-date=11 December 2025 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwkpNd2ceBk&t=453s}}</ref>

In March 2022 she extended the world record to 100 trillion digits of pi.<ref name=Iwao2022/>
